Upstream genesys, before and after

The same colour negative on the same OpticFilm 8200i (07b3:1825), scanned once with upstream SANE (genesys, master 982deaef) and once with the same driver with patched seven patches applied. Both go through the identical negative conversion, so what you see differs only because the raw data differs. The patches bring genesys closer to the plustek8200i backend compared on the earlier page.

1 · Whole frame, 600 dpi

Both scans are drawn on one shared film coordinate system, so the same piece of film lies in the same place in every view. Dark areas are where a scan window did not reach. White areas are inside a window but beyond the film (unexposed film inverts to white).

patchedupstream

Drag anywhere on the picture, or focus the handle and use the arrow keys.

upstream

patched

Zoom with the buttons above, then scroll: both panels move together.

patched

Click the picture or press Space to flip between the two. Whatever moves is a difference.

2 · Scan area

Distance in millimetres between the film's edge and the edge of the scan window, measured the same way on both scans (the half-brightness point between the holder and the film). A value near zero means the film touches the window edge and a small positioning error would clip the picture.

600 dpileftrighttopbottom
upstream0.810.010.390.14
patched0.470.351.691.10
3600 dpi
upstream0.850.060.410.16
patched0.500.411.811.06
What changed. Upstream's window sat 0.34 mm too far toward one edge, so the film touched the window's right-hand edge and was cut off there, and it left 0.1–0.4 mm above and below the frame. The patched window is centred (0.5 mm either side) and leaves 1.1–1.8 mm above and below. The film measures the same size in both scans (35.75 × 24.30 mm), so the holder was not disturbed between them.

3 · Colour and calibration

Upstream programs the gain codes SilverFast used in its own captures. On this unit they saturate the empty-gate reading that the shading table is built from. The patched driver reads the lit gate at gain 0 and chooses each channel's gain so the brightest column reaches 87 % of full scale.

White strip, 3600 dpiupstream (columns at the ADC ceiling)patched (columns at the ADC ceiling)
Red62,981–63,077  (5181 / 5184)42,315–55,063  (0 / 5184)
Green62,980–62,981  (5184 / 5184)43,695–55,412  (0 / 5184)
Blue62,579–62,579  (5184 / 5184)43,598–55,757  (0 / 5184)
Gain codes (R, G, B)39, 32, 39 (fixed)21, 2, 13 (from the lit gate: 40,658, 55,069, 47,168)
Rendered, centre of frameupstreampatched  (plustek8200i)
Median R / G / B35,664 / 16,868 / 11,82027,568 / 11,115 / 7,749  (24,109 / 9,794 / 7,410)
G / R, B / R0.473, 0.3310.403, 0.281  (0.406, 0.307)
What this means. Upstream's white strip is a flat line at the ceiling: every column the same, so the shading table has nothing to flatten and the lamp's fall-off is left in the picture. The patched strip spans a real profile (about 23 % darker at the edges, close to the 1.25–1.3× seen with the other backend) and the table can correct it. The output is less bright and less green, and its colour ratios (G/R 0.403, B/R 0.281) are close to the other backend's (0.406, 0.307).

4 · Detail at 3600 dpi

The same physical area cut from each 3600 dpi scan (1000×750 pixels), lined up on the film's own corner. Drag to wipe between them.

patchedupstream

The girl's face and a tulip

patchedupstream

The large, soft-focus tulip

patchedupstream

Flowers and soil at the bottom

Sharpness is unchanged. The patches do not touch the optics or the scanning speed: the same grain and the same dust specks appear in both. The change is in what the image is made of around them: the calibration, the area and the colour balance. The extra detail you gain is the film that was previously outside the window.

5 · Infrared, as a second frame

With --infra-red set the driver delivers the image as two frames: the colour scan, then an infrared plane of the same area. Upstream has no infrared at all for this scanner. This is one two-frame scan; both views are aligned as the driver delivered them, with no registration applied. The two-frame sequence is the paired-frames convention proposed in The Fourth Channel, our survey of how SANE backends handle infrared.

sane_control_option(h, infra-red, yes)
before start:  format=RGB   last_frame=0   864x640
frame 1:       format=RGB   last_frame=0   864x640  depth=16   (read to the end)
frame 2:       format=GRAY  last_frame=1   864x640  depth=16   (second sane_start, no sane_cancel between)
Drag to wipe between the colour frame and its infrared frame, whole frame at 600 dpi.
infraredimage

In the infrared frame the film dye disappears and only physical defects remain: dust, hairs and scratches. The dark edge at the left is the film holder.

infraredimage

A scratch and torn emulsion on the right-hand side

infraredimage

Dust specks and a hair between the stems

How well do the frames line up? At 3600 dpi the scratches and dust in the infrared frame coincide with the visible ones to within 2 pixels (0.015 mm) in five regions of this scan (cross-correlation of the visible defects against the infrared defect map; vertical offsets −0.3 to +0.6 pixel, horizontal −0.9 to +1.8). The two frames are two passes of the carriage, and separate scans of this scanner repeat less well (about 0.1 mm), so the man page tells frontends to verify the alignment rather than assume it.

6 · The patches

Seven patches against SANE master 982deaef. Apply them with git am docs/upstream-genesys-patches/*.patch. Each is a separate commit; the series builds and passes upstream's genesys unit tests.

#PatchLines
1Cover the whole film gate on the OpticFilm 8200i SE The default window clipped the film at the right-hand edge and left 0.1–0.4 mm above and below the frame. The window now covers the whole gate with the film centred.gl128.cpp, tables_model.cpp+16 −12patch
2Choose the front-end gain from the lit gate SilverFast's fixed front-end gain drove the white strip to the ADC ceiling on this unit, so the shading table was built from clipped data. The gain is now chosen per channel from the lit gate.gl128.cpp+43 −2patch
3Offer 8-bit output on the OpticFilm 8200i SE --depth 8 for Color and Gray. The ASIC still scans at 16 bits; the high byte is kept at the end of the pipeline.gl128.cpp, low.cpp, tables_model.cpp, tests_gl128.cpp+34 −7patch
4Add the infrared scan source of the OpticFilm 8200i SE The Transparency Adapter Infrared source, as the other genesys film scanners offer it: a standalone gray image of the infrared plane.gl128.cpp, tables_model.cpp, tables_sensor.cpp, tests_gl128.cpp+81 −23patch
5Report the IntelliScan and QuickScan buttons IntelliScan and QuickScan as the sensor options extra and scan, read from the interrupt endpoint. A physical press has not been verified through genesys yet.gl128.cpp, tables_model.cpp, test_usb_device.cpp, test_usb_device.h, usb_device.cpp, usb_device.h+58 −3patch
6Document the OpticFilm 8200i SE improvements The genesys.desc entry and a newsfragment.genesys.desc, genesys_gl128_8200i_se_parity.backend+2 −2patch
7Add the infra-red option: the infrared plane as a second frame --infra-red: the standard option name. The image frame, then a gray frame of the same area from a second sane_start, with no cancel between.genesys.cpp, genesys.h, sane-genesys.man, genesys_gl128_8200i_se_parity.backend+156 −4patch

7 · What is not fixed

  • Speed. At 3600 dpi genesys takes about 53 s against 34.6 s for plustek8200i. It samples the film twice per output line and averages, following SilverFast's captured motor ramp. Halving the line count alone changed the vertical scale instead of the time, so the motor and line-period registers would have to be worked out again.
  • Exposure multiplier (--exposure) for dense negatives, for the same reason.
  • Dust removal and white balance (--ir-clean, --auto-wb) are host-side processing that genesys has no place for. --infra-red gives a frontend what it needs to do dust removal itself.
  • Buttons. The option names and the endpoint read are verified; a physical press through genesys is not.
  • Other scanners. --infra-red is written for every genesys model with an infrared scan method (CanoScan 8400F and 8600F, OpticFilm 7200i, 7500i, 8200i) but was tested only on the 8200i SE.
  • One unit, one frame. These are single-scanner, single-frame results.

How this was made. Same frame in the holder, scanned on 2026-10-21 with an OpticFilm 8200i (USB 07b3:1825). Upstream: SANE master 982deaef, genesys only. Patched: the same tree with the seven patches (63d8cb16). Both raw 16-bit scans went through the same nv-cli render negative conversion with each scan's own film-base estimate and no dust removal. The detail crops are aligned on the film's measured top-left corner. Margins are measured on the raw scans; the infrared frames come from a separate two-frame scan of the same frame. The page is built by tools/build-genesys-patches-page.py.

Where to go next. The patches, the earlier comparison and the plustek8200i backend live in the OpticFilm8200i-sane repository. Upstreaming is tracked in SANE backends work item #886.
